# The focus round

The binding specification of the focus round, written 2026-09-15 by the round's synthesizer from the seven production audits under `docs/gslides-parity/focus/` (`audit-decks.md`, `audit-slides.md`, `audit-text.md`, `audit-images.md`, `audit-arrange.md`, `audit-shapes.md` with `audit-orchestrator-shapes.md`, `audit-present.md`, `audit-export.md`), the sales research (`docs/gslides-parity/research/07-sales-users.md`), the last production walk (`docs/gslides-parity/build-4/hotfix-4.md` sections 1.3 and 3.8) and the menu model, toolbar and palette sources of the production commit, and revised the same day against the two judgments `docs/gslides-parity/focus/judge-sales.md` and `docs/gslides-parity/focus/judge-reliability.md`. Production is https://turboslide.vercel.app serving `ec61c6b`. Every file and line cited below is read from that commit (`git show ec61c6b:<path>`) unless the sentence says otherwise; the shared checkout is on `main` at `d5a1be5`, one commit behind production, and its working tree carries round five's uncommitted edits to many of the same files, so its line numbers differ.

Every audit drove production through the product's own controls with headless Chromium at 1440 by 900 at human speed, on scratch decks created from `/new` and trashed and deleted forever afterwards; each audit's method section records this. A row in an audit is "works", "broken", "flaky" (it passed on a later try or on another deck) or "not driven" with the reason. This document keeps those four words and no others for a row's state. It reports what happened; a step nobody drove is not driven, never passed.

The matrix of section 6 is data: `docs/gslides-parity/focus/core-matrix.json`. This document is rendered from that file and from the prose in `docs/gslides-parity/focus/focus-body.md` by `docs/gslides-parity/focus/render-focus.mjs` (`node docs/gslides-parity/focus/render-focus.mjs`, then prettier); the table of section 6.4, every count of section 6.3, the held list of section 7 and the by feature reading of rule 4 are rendered, never typed. The matrix holds 856 rows.

## 1. Kevin's directive and the rule it sets

Kevin's directive of 2026-09-15, verbatim: "i think there are a bunch of features that donnt work like shapes. we can get rid of those for now and focus on teh features we need, that work, and that work well with every interaction tested." His standing words: "remember this is actually going to be used by majority sales in our org"; "make sure to actually test our slide features and make sure they work".

The rule this round sets, and every later round keeps:

A feature is in the product's default view only when every one of its interactions works on production and is in the test matrix.

What the rule means in practice:

1. "Works" means the interaction's matrix row passes when the row is driven against the preview and against production (section 6). An interaction that was never driven is not driven, and a feature with a not driven interaction is not in the default view until the row is driven and passes.
2. The default view is the core set of section 2: what a seller does weekly, per `07-sales-users.md` (the paragraph after the population table: "the sales user opens a deck that already exists, duplicates or deletes slides, replaces a logo or screenshot, retypes a name and a few numbers, reorders, hides the slides that do not apply, presents over a call, and sends a PDF or a link"). Everything else on production today is the parked set of section 3.
3. Parked means hidden behind one switch, Tools > Advanced tools, never deleted. A parked feature's rows leave the menu bar, the toolbar, the right click menus, Search the menus and the shortcuts dialog while the switch is off; its blocks still render when a deck carries them; its actions stay on the CLI, MCP, HTTP and window transports and are documented as advanced.
4. A core interaction that is broken or flaky today is fixed in this round (section 5). Every matrix row carries a `feature` field naming its section 2 feature, and the run computes from the file which features have a not driven or failed row; such a feature is parked for that ship and the ship note's parked list is rendered from the run, not typed. The switch itself (`surface.*`) is the mechanism of parking and cannot be parked: a failed or not driven `surface.*` row blocks the ship.
5. Nothing enters the default view by being built. It enters by its rows joining the matrix and passing on production first (section 8).

The audits behind this document, all on `ec61c6b` on 2026-09-15: decks 61 rows (`audit-decks.md`), slides 107 rows (`audit-slides.md`), text 61 rows (`audit-text.md`), pictures 67 rows (`audit-images.md`), arrange 78 rows (`audit-arrange.md`), shapes 50 rows of which 31 were driven (rows 1 to 30 and 35), rows 31 to 34 not driven because production draws the gallery plate where the named rows would be, and rows 36 to 50 not driven because the orchestrator's stop arrived at row 35 (`audit-shapes.md`; 15 is the count of presets inserted by click, row 24), present and share 50 rows (`audit-present.md`), export 51 rows (`audit-export.md`). The last full production walk was 802 steps, 778 ok, 23 failed (all the picture frame W7) and 1 not driven, against production serving `e2e6307` (`hotfix-4.md` section 3.8); `ec61c6b` changed `packages/store/src/blob-store.ts`, `packages/store/src/comments-store.ts` and `packages/store/src/migrate.ts` after it (`git diff --stat e2e6307 ec61c6b`), so the walk's rows are the last observation of what they drove and not an observation of `ec61c6b`.

## 2. The core set

One entry per feature a seller needs weekly. Each entry names the menu rows by their `data-control` id in `packages/chrome/src/menus/model.ts` (the id is the `MenuItem.id`, `model.ts` line 393; line numbers below are `ec61c6b`'s), the toolbar controls by their `data-control` id in `TOOLBAR_HEAD` (`model.ts` 2292), `TOOLBAR_TAIL_DEFAULT` (`model.ts` 2357) and `packages/chrome/src/menus/toolbar-tails.ts`, the right click rows by the `CONTEXT_MENUS` target that carries them (`model.ts` 2505), the shortcuts as the model prints them, and the interactions by their matrix id (section 6). The matrix's `feature` key of each entry is in parentheses after the heading. Search the menus lists every menu row that is present as a palette row carrying `data-control="palette.<row id>"` (`packages/chrome/src/Palette.tsx`, the results list under `data-control="palette"` at line 254 and the query field `palette.query` at 310; the rows come from `finderRows` in `packages/chrome/src/menus/finder.ts` 42 to 65; the `menus` and `layouts` groups are `packages/chrome/src/palette-data.ts` 46 to 53), so a feature's palette entries are its menu rows and the 21 layout rows, and no separate list is kept here.

The seller opens a deck that exists, names the tailored copy after the customer, makes the customer copy without the talk track, and never loses work (`07-sales-users.md` rows "Start a new deck", "Make a customer-facing copy", "Never lose work", design rules 1, 9 and 19).

- Rows: `title.appIcon` (the mark, back to /decks), `title.name` (click to rename; Enter keeps, Escape restores), `title.saveState` (the save words), `title.lastEdit` (opens Version history, Cmd+Option+Shift+H), `file.new.presentation`, `file.rename`, `file.moveToTrash`, `file.makeCopy.entire` with its dialog's Remove speaker notes checkbox (`packages/chrome/src/dialogs/MakeCopy.tsx` 105 to 110), `file.versionHistory.see`, `file.versionHistory.nameCurrent` (`model.ts` 646 to 700, 801 to 812 and 875 to 914). The card menu on /decks is the home page's own menu with the seven rows Open, Open in new tab, Present, Rename, Make a copy, Download and Move to trash (`audit-decks` row 33); the trash page has Restore and Delete forever (`audit-decks` rows 49 to 53).
- Toolbar: none beyond the title row.
- Interactions: `decks.*` in the matrix, from `decks.home.new-presentation` to `decks.notfound.page`, with `decks.card.download` and `decks.file.make-a-copy` added in this revision.
- Today: the whole path from /home to a saved deck works, every title row rename path works, Present, Download, Move to trash with Undo, Restore and Delete forever work (`audit-decks` summary "What works", line 11). The card Rename, the row Rename, Make a copy on the deck just edited and the listing after Restore do not (section 5). File > Make a copy from the editor and its checkbox were not driven (5.1).

## 3. The parked set

Every other feature on production today. Parked features are hidden, not disabled, and nothing is deleted. Where the research's task table names a parked feature, the entry says which row it departs from, so each departure reads as chosen.

### 3.1 The switch

- One row, `tools.advancedTools`, label "Advanced tools", in the Tools menu after `tools.checkSlides` (`model.ts` 2091 to 2097) and before the existing `tools.advanced` submenu (`model.ts` 2098 to 2145, itself parked), built as `now('tools.advancedTools', 'Advanced tools', toggle('advancedTools'), { turboslide: true })` with a checkbox and one sentence of tooltip naming what it shows.
- One `MenuSetting`, `advancedTools`, added to the union at `model.ts` 216 to 245; off in `DEFAULT_SETTINGS` (`editor-shell.ts` 2732); remembered the way the other browser kept settings are, by joining `STORED_SETTINGS` (`editor-shell.ts` 2716 to 2724) under the `ts-editor-settings` key (`editor-shell.ts` 2713) that `readStoredSettings` and `writeStoredSettings` handle (`editor-shell.ts` 2767 and 2784; the shell reads them at `EditorShell.tsx` 341 and writes them at 458 to 461). Production's action table has no preferences record (zero matches for `prefs` in `git show ec61c6b:packages/schema/src/actions.ts`), so the setting is per browser today; when round five's preferences record lands the setting follows the principal and the browser copy is the fallback.
- One flag on the model's rows, `advanced?: true`, on `MenuItem` beside `turboslide` and `contextOnly` (`model.ts` 430 to 433) and on `ToolbarControl` beside its `turboslide` (`model.ts` 2283 to 2284). The one function that decides presence is `isPresent` (`model.ts` 2984 to 2986); after the change it returns false for a row or control carrying `advanced: true` and for a row whose `status` is `later` while `ctx.settings.advancedTools` is not true, and otherwise reads `when` as today. That is the whole decision on the Later stubs: `isPresent` reads `status === 'later'` under the switch, and no stub carries `advanced: true`, so there is one predicate. This departs from the parity rounds' rule that a Later row stands disabled in Google's position (`model.ts` 14 to 17): a disabled row gives the seller nothing, and Search the menus stays clean (the sales judgment's note on the question). A parent whose children are all absent is absent; a menu whose rows are all absent is not drawn (the Extensions menu with the switch off).

## 4. The shapes decision

Decision: a minimal set is kept and made to work in every interaction: Rectangle, Rounded rectangle and Ellipse as shape presets with hand written paths, Line and Arrow as line blocks, each with fill, border and text where the kind takes them. The four galleries, the block arrows, the callouts, the equation signs, Change shape and Mask image are parked until the geometry interpreter draws them and passes the canvas fidelity gate. Insert > Shape > Shapes lists Rectangle, Rounded rectangle and Ellipse as named rows and Insert > Line lists Line and Arrow.

The evidence:

1. Every preset draws as its bounding rectangle. `shapePath` in `packages/schema/src/shapes.ts` returns `M0,0 H{w} V{h} H0 Z` for every kind (lines 385 to 393 at `ec61c6b`), the docblock at 395 says "the whole box until the interpreter lands", the renderer's preset branch calls it (`packages/render/src/blocks/primitives.ts` 321 and 484), and the picker draws every glyph from `shapePath(48, 36)` (`packages/chrome/src/pickers/ShapePicker.tsx` 22 to 26) (`audit-orchestrator-shapes.md`). On production the 135 tiles of the four galleries were the same 28 by 21 px rectangle outline with the name only in a hover tooltip (`audit-shapes` rows 4 to 8, screenshots `01` to `04`), and the triangle, diamond, hexagon, star, cloud, right arrow, left right arrow, chevron, both callouts and both equation signs inserted as hairline rectangles carrying the right `data-shape` (`audit-shapes` rows 12 to 23 and 27 to 30). Only the rectangle and the ellipse drew their own outline (rows 9, 11, 25, 26). A seller who picks a callout and gets a box is worse off than a seller who finds no callout (`audit-shapes` summary, line 13).
2. The gallery counts on production (99, 26, 4, 6) differ from the shape table at `ec61c6b` (100, 20, 10, 6) (`audit-shapes` rows 4 to 7), so the built plate is not the table in the source.
3. The rounded rectangle's radius was not measured on production (`audit-shapes` row 10 recorded works with the radius unconfirmed) and cannot exist while `shapePath` returns the box; it needs its own path, as does any block arrow (`audit-orchestrator-shapes.md`, "Consequences"). The matrix row `shapes.insert.rounded-click` is therefore not driven, with the source reading in its evidence cell.
4. A fresh shape has no fill and a `var(--hair)` 1 px stroke, a faint outline on the dark theme (`audit-shapes` row 35, severity 1).
5. The battery on the kept kinds is not driven on `ec61c6b`. The shapes audit was stopped at row 35 before select, move, resize, rotate, fill, border, text, duplicate, delete, undo, Format options, lines, connectors, the exports and the reload (`audit-shapes` rows 36 to 49, each "not driven" with the reason). The production walk of hotfix 4, against `e2e6307`, passed the rectangle's move, its eight handles plain, with Shift and with Alt, the ring, Cmd+D, Delete, Cmd+Z and Cmd+Shift+Z (`hotfix-4.md` section 3.8, rows 771 to 782 and the rectangle's resize rows, none of which failed), and a line drawn by a drag with its end drag (row 54); those observations predate `ec61c6b` and the matrix records the rows as not driven with the walk as the last observation. No walk has driven fill, border, text in a shape, the arrow's head, the line tail or a shape through the exports (`audit-shapes` rows 40 to 42, 45 to 48). Only `shapes.select` was driven on `ec61c6b` (`audit-arrange` row 1 clicked a rectangle: chip "Shape", eight handles, the ring).
6. The named rows already exist in the model (`insert.shape.shapes.rectangle`, `.rounded`, `.ellipse`, `insert.shape.arrows.arrow`, `model.ts` 1217 to 1236) but production draws the `shapes` plate instead because the submenus carry `effect: shapeGrid(...)` (`model.ts` 1227 and 1237); the audit could not click a named row (`audit-shapes` rows 31 to 34).

What the minimal set requires before it ships in the default view: a rounded rectangle path and an ellipse path in `shapePath` for those two kinds (the rectangle keeps the box path), the `shapes` plate effect removed from `insert.shape.shapes` so the three named rows draw, `insert.shape.arrows` parked, a visible default look (a fill from the theme, or a stroke that reads on both themes), a text run opened by Enter or a double click on a shape (`audit-shapes` row 42: a fresh shape has no run), and every `shapes.*` and `lines.*` matrix row passing on the preview and on production. If any `shapes.*` row is not passing by the ship, the whole of Insert > Shape leaves the default view for that ship and the `lines` feature stands alone when its own rows pass; if a `lines.*` row is not passing, Line and Arrow leave too. The reasoning is Kevin's ("we can get rid of those for now") and the rule of section 1. The block arrow returns with the interpreter (SPEC-5 6.5, `docs/gslides-parity/SPEC-5.md` line 498), not before. The sales judgment's note that a rectangle and an ellipse without the rounded rectangle are worth keeping is recorded; the rule still parks the feature whole when one of its rows fails (section 8), so the rounded path is part of the work, not optional. At the first ship of the round Insert > Shape and Insert > Line left the default view under this rule (the parking edit landed in b1's cycle 2 on 2026-09-16, on the evidence of the verifier's pass 2: 4 of 20 `shapes.*` rows and 1 of 5 `lines.*` rows failed on the enforce preview and none had passed on production); the rows stay in the matrix with their drivers, the walk drives them with Tools > Advanced tools on as the evidence for their return, the ship's parked list names `shapes` and `lines`, and the two features return whole under section 8.

## 5. The broken and flaky core interactions, ranked

Severity as the audits define it: 3 the seller cannot complete a top task, 2 a wrong or lost result, 1 cosmetic. Owner names the area of the code and the person who fixes it: "text and slides" is the text runs, the filmstrip and the layouts (`packages/viewer/src/Editor.tsx`'s text paths, `packages/schema/src/apply-layout.ts`, the filmstrip) and the text and slides builder; "objects" is the canvas objects, the handles, the pictures and the shapes (`packages/viewer`, `packages/render`) and the objects builder; "surface" is the menu model, the toolbar, the dialogs and the home page (`packages/chrome`, `apps/studio/src/routes`) and the surface builder; "server" is the server functions, the store, the sync engine and authorization (`apps/studio/src/server`, `packages/store`, `packages/realtime`) and the integrator. The matrix ids are section 6's. Every row here is broken or flaky; the not driven rows are 5.1.

The refusals are the `RangeError`s of `packages/schema/src/reduce.ts` 55 and 187. The tab's revision equalled the server revision before each refused write (the `sync` facts in rows 93 and 95), so the instance that refused held a document behind the revision it had acknowledged; on the blob tier presence, locks and the mirror are per instance and the mirror follows a one second head poll (`packages/realtime/src/blob.ts` 1 to 10; `packages/store/src/blob-store.ts` 494 to 500 on the lagging body), which is the reading the audit called a hypothesis. The reproduction step: on production, delete a slide, wait for "All changes saved", press Cmd+Z, and read on every write answer a header `x-turboslide-revision` naming the instance's document revision beside the request's `baseRevision`; the refusal body gains the same two numbers, and the probe records both on every refused write. The fix: a write applies only against the store's head document (`head()` and the body whose md5 matches the etag, `blob-store.ts` 494 to 500), never against the instance's mirror. ### 5.1 The not driven core rows, and who drives them before the ship

Every not driven core row is driven before the ship by the person named, on the preview and on production, through the driver the matrix names; a row still not driven at the ship parks its feature (rule 4), and the second column of each group names the menu rows that leave the default view with it. ## 6. The test matrix

Every core interaction is a row with a stable id, `area.feature.interaction`, and a `feature` field. The matrix is the file `docs/gslides-parity/focus/core-matrix.json`; the table of 6.4 is rendered from it and the file is the source when the two differ. Every row records what production did on 2026-09-15 ("Today on production") and names the audit row or the file that saw it; a row the audits measured carries its time bound in the interaction text, so the pass criterion is fixed before the run and not chosen after it (5 s for a picture to land, 5 s for a listing, 5 s three of three for collaboration, 20 s for a comment, 30 s for a download).

### 6.1 What drives a row

- `probe --core`: `scripts/probes/editor-walk-probe.mjs` gains a `--core` flag beside `--base`, `--json`, `--shots`, `--quick` and `--headed` (lines 52 to 66). In `--core` mode a `step()` call that proves a matrix row carries the row's id as a tag (the `record` and `step` helpers at lines 78 to 104 gain the tag and write it as `id` in the JSON row); an untagged step is a setup step and runs as today. When a setup step fails, every later tagged step that depends on it is recorded as not driven with the reason "setup failed: <step>", and the run exits 1 (the cascade `audit-arrange` section 1 records, where run 3's rows after the paste row failed because the stage held another slide, becomes a not driven reason and a failed run, never a false failure of the dependent rows). A matrix id whose driver is `probe --core` and for which the run finds no tagged step is a failure of the run ("no step" exits 1), not a not driven row. The exit code is 1 when any tagged step fails or is not driven, unless the row's feature is in the ship's committed parked list (6.2). The walk keeps its human pace, its scratch deck from `/new` and its `finally` block (File > Move to trash, Delete forever, the 404, lines 3164 to 3243). As built (b4.md section 1.1, 2.1): `--core` runs its own walk over the parity walk's helpers, pace, scratch deck and `finally` block (`scripts/probes/core-walk/`, one module per area), not tags on the 800 step parity walk; `scripts/probes/core-gate.mjs` runs the probe and the core specs against one base and merges every row by id, and against a localhost base it takes `.turboslide/e2e.lock` itself for the whole run, so a caller never holds the lock while it runs; a run against a deployment needs no lock. A row the orchestrator's ruling (3) marks manual carries `manual: <the obstacle>` in the matrix and a step in `docs/gslides-parity/focus/manual-checklist.md`; a run records it as not driven with that reason, never as passed, and it parks no feature and fails no ship.
- `core/<area>.spec.ts`: Playwright specs under `apps/studio/e2e/core/`, run from the repository root with `PLAYWRIGHT_BASE_URL=<origin>` so the config defines no web server (`playwright.config.ts` 19 to 20 and 34 to 36), one worker (27), retries 0 (28), viewport 1440 by 900 (32). These carry the rows the probe cannot drive in one tab: the file chooser and the clipboard picture (`core/images.spec.ts`), two browser contexts (`core/share.spec.ts`, `core/present.spec.ts`, `core/slides.spec.ts` for the two tab paste), files checked on disk (`core/export.spec.ts`), the list and trash surfaces (`core/decks.spec.ts`) and the switch (`core/surface.spec.ts`). The rules for a core spec, so that it runs against production as written: no import from `node:fs` except to read a file the browser downloaded; no deck seeded from disk or from a fixture; no environment variable read other than `PLAYWRIGHT_BASE_URL` and `VERCEL_OIDC_TOKEN`; every observation through the page, `window.turboslide.studio.describe()`, the network and the download; every deck created from `/new` by the test itself and torn down in `afterEach` and in a `finally` through File > Move to trash, Delete forever on `/decks/trash` and a 404 check on `/edit/<id>`. The existing specs are not the pattern: `apps/studio/e2e/home.spec.ts` 272 to 338 reads the manifest from disk (`manifestOf`, `existsSync(join(DECKS, ...))`), `present.spec.ts` 16 to 45 seeds `decks/e2e-present` from a fixture, and `share.spec.ts` 24 decides its refusal rows from the runner's own `TURBOSLIDE_AUTHORIZE`; a core spec observes the production it is pointed at and nothing else. No spec clicks Empty trash (`audit-decks` row 54) or touches a deck it did not create. A setup write through the window API (the matrix's `setup` field: `block.insert` of a parked block, `deck.set` of the appearance) is made before the driven steps and is never counted as one.
- On a preview the probe and the specs send `VERCEL_OIDC_TOKEN` as `x-vercel-trusted-oidc-idp-token` (the probe's line 66); on production they send nothing. Under `.turboslide/e2e.lock`, one run at a time. Two preview only arrangements of the drivers step around Vercel Authentication and never around the product: the card Download's bytes are fetched with the OIDC header from the URL the page's click started when the browser's download is redirected by the wall, and the hero row removes `/home`'s speculation rules before the click on a preview; production and localhost run both rows as written (b4 FR4). A dev server a lane measures against runs on the watcher blind config `apps/studio/vite.no-watch.config.ts`, so another lane's save cannot remount the page mid run (b3 R22).

### 6.2 Acceptance

- The parked list is committed before the runs: `docs/gslides-parity/focus/ship-<commit>.json` with `{ "commit": "<sha>", "parkedFeatures": [...] }`. A run exits 1 when any core id is failed or not driven unless its feature is in that list; the `surface` feature cannot be listed.
- Before a ship, every core row of every feature not in the parked list passes on the preview built from the ship's commit and on production after the alias moves. A row with several checks (the eight handles, the two theme colours, the two decks of the card paste) passes only when every check passes.
- The run ledger: the ship note lists every run started against the preview and against production on the ship's commit, with its start time, origin, commit, deck id, counts and JSON path; no run is left out. A row passes only when it passes in the last run of each origin. A rerun happens only after a code change, named by its commit, or with a reason written in the ledger; a row that fails in one run and passes in a later run on a fresh deck with no code change between them is flaky and fails the ship. `retries` stays 0 (`playwright.config.ts` 28), no core spec calls `test.describe.configure({ retries })`, and the report's retry count is asserted to be zero. This is what closes the gap the audits saw between decks and runs (`audit-images` row 6 passed on two decks and broke on `3fma`; `audit-present` row 31 delivered in 2.4 s in run 2 and lost three edits in run 3; `audit-decks` row 37 failed three times on one card and passed on a fresh one).
- Not driven rows are listed in the ship note by id and reason and are never counted as passed; the ship note's parked list is rendered from the run's JSON by feature.
- `node scripts/probes/new-write-probe.mjs --base <origin>` and `node scripts/hosted-smoke.mjs <origin>` keep running as they did for hotfix 4 (`hotfix-4.md` section 3.8).

### 6.3 The counts, rendered from the file

The matrix holds 856 rows. By what production did on 2026-09-15: 360 works, 224 broken, 26 flaky, 246 not driven. By driver: 609 probe --core, 51 core/decks.spec.ts, 45 core/export.spec.ts, 30 core/present.spec.ts, 30 core/share.spec.ts, 14 core/images.spec.ts, 12 core/svg.spec.ts, 11 core/brand.spec.ts, 10 core/sync.spec.ts, 10 core/shaders.spec.ts, 8 core/logos.spec.ts, 6 core/surface.spec.ts, 6 cost-probe, 5 core/chrome.spec.ts, 5 core/assist.spec.ts, 3 core/documents.spec.ts, 1 core/slides.spec.ts. The failed rows by severity, as the audits set it: 76 at severity 3, 109 at severity 2, 65 at severity 1; a not driven row carries no severity. 68 rows name a setup write that is not a driven step.

By feature, with the reading rule 4 of section 1 gives on today's data (a feature with a not driven or failed row would be parked at a ship made today; the switch itself is the mechanism of parking and a failed or not driven `surface.*` row blocks the ship instead):

## 7. The README section "What works today"

The text below is the README for the ship, to replace the "Feature tour" of `README.md` (lines 46 to 312) as the first section after the introduction, in plain technical English, with no count typed by hand; the counts a reader wants are the matrix's and are rendered from `core-matrix.json`, never typed. It is rendered from the matrix: a feature's paragraph appears only while every row of that feature passes on production, and a feature with a failed or not driven row is listed as held with the rows that hold it. The 135 preset claim at `README.md` 146 and 404 leaves with the first ship. One sentence holds across the outputs once `export.pdf.file`, `export.pptx.perfect`, `present.skipped-left-out`, `share.view-link-excludes-skipped-and-notes` and `share.present-link-excludes-skipped` pass: skipped slides and speaker notes stay out of the PDF, the PowerPoint file, the show and the view link unless the seller checks the box that includes them; until then the sentence is not in the README.

> ## What works today
>
> Turboslide is a slide editor for a team that tailors an existing deck and presents it. Every feature in the default view is driven end to end against the production deployment before a release, at human speed, and the release note carries the table of what passed. Features that are not yet tested that way are behind Tools > Advanced tools and are documented as advanced.
>
> (Rendered from `core-matrix.json` on 2026-09-15: no feature has every row passing on production today, so this section holds no feature paragraph until the ship. The paragraphs below are the drafts each feature earns once every row it names passes.)

The paragraphs held until every row of their feature passes, with the rows that hold them today:

- 2.1 Decks and the home surfaces (`decks`), held by 25 of 64 rows: `decks.new.ground-paint`, `decks.title.tab-title-after-rename`, `decks.save.acknowledged`, `decks.card.rename-enter`, `decks.row.rename-enter`, `decks.card.make-a-copy`, `decks.card.open-in-new-tab`, `decks.trash.listed-after-move`, `decks.trash.lists-after-restore`, `decks.trash.delete-forever-enter`, `decks.access.paint`, `decks.file.make-a-copy`, `decks.name.follows-heading`, `decks.recent.drops-trashed`, `decks.trash.editor-undo-snackbar`, `decks.recent.this-browser-sentence`, `decks.home.seller-lead`, `decks.card.thumbnail-slide-1`, `decks.card.edited-relative-time`, `decks.card.more-glyph`, `decks.trash.button-heights`, `decks.trash.confirm-dialog-chrome`, `decks.new.skeleton-one-frame`, `decks.access.stranger-links`, `decks.notfound.sentence-case`.
  Held paragraph: **Decks.** The root address opens a new presentation. The first edit saves it and every later edit saves itself; the title row says so. Rename the deck in the title row or from File. The home page lists your presentations with search, opens a deck from its card, and the card menu presents, renames, copies, downloads and trashes. File > Make a copy makes the customer copy with or without the speaker notes. The trash restores a deck or deletes it forever after one confirmation.
- 2.2 Slides and the filmstrip (`slides`), held by 18 of 85 rows: `slides.delete.two-selected-menu`, `slides.delete.two-selected-edit-menu`, `slides.delete.canvas-focus-undo`, `slides.delete.undo-redo-saved`, `slides.layout.fresh-slide-two-picks-no-carry`, `slides.layout.snackbar-counts-typed-only`, `slides.clipboard.copy-paste-card`, `slides.reorder.menu-up-down-beginning`, `slides.reorder.cmd-shift-up-down`, `slides.notes.view-menu-toggle`, `slides.context.empty-canvas`, `slides.numbers.apply`, `slides.layout.title-and-body-single`, `slides.layout.subtitle-prompt`, `slides.layout.new-slide-inherits`, `slides.layout.tile-sentences`, `slides.layout.plate-four-columns`, `slides.import.none-preselected`.
  Held paragraph: **Slides.** New slide from the toolbar, the Slide menu, the right click menu or Ctrl+M adds a slide after the current one with the same layout; the arrow beside it picks a layout. Duplicate, delete and skip work on one slide or a selection, from the filmstrip, the menu or the keyboard, and each undoes. Drag a card to reorder, move it with the keyboard, or copy and paste a slide within a deck or into another. Apply layout offers the theme's layouts and moves only what you typed. Speaker notes sit under the slide and show in Presenter view.
- 2.3 Text (`text`), held by 47 of 91 rows: `text.title.single-click`, `text.selected.typing-replaces`, `text.selected.enter-appends`, `text.title.double-click-enters`, `text.textbox.drag-inside-moves`, `text.textbox.burst-reliability`, `text.italic.toolbar-word`, `text.color.swatch-on-word`, `text.list.bulleted-toolbar`, `text.list.numbered-toolbar`, `text.link.cmd-k-enter`, `text.link.present-click`, `text.format-menu.text-fitting`, `text.autofit.textbox-grow`, `text.clipboard.paste-without-formatting`, `text.find-replace.shortcut`, `text.list.numbered-menu-preset`, `text.list.chords`, `text.link.toolbar-button`, `text.format-options.panel`, `text.layout-runs.type`, `text.context.text-block`, `text.context.text-selection`, `text.context.inside-session`, `text.format-menu.size-decrease`, `text.format-menu.spacing-single-1-15`, `text.format-menu.align-indent-rows`, `text.textbox.toolbar-button`, `text.title.one-click-tail`, `text.title.bold-menu`, `text.title.bold-cmd-b`, `text.title.align-menu`, `text.title.size-menu`, `text.title.format-options-marks`, `text.title.apply-layout-after-format`, `text.fontsize.type-one-undo`, `text.format-options.field-one-undo`, `text.link.detect-url`, `text.link.detect-email`, `text.select.double-click-address`, `text.select.shift-home-line`, `text.link.popover-apply-remove`, `text.link.slide-target`, `text.format-options.padding-grid`, `text.format-options.remembers-section`, `text.autofit.shrink-on-overflow`, `text.find-replace.count-while-typing`.
  Held paragraph: **Text.** Click a placeholder and type. Bold, italic, underline and strikethrough apply to a selected word from the keyboard or the toolbar. Font size, alignment, line spacing, bulleted and numbered lists, indent and clear formatting are on the toolbar and in the Format menu. Cmd+K or the toolbar button links a word. Find and replace renames a customer across the deck. Cut, copy and paste work within a box, between boxes and between slides; Cmd+Shift+V pastes plain text.

## 8. What stays for later

- The parked set of section 3, whole. The rows that already passed their audit (Group, Ungroup, Distribute, Rotate 90, Show ruler, the guides, Snap to; `audit-arrange` rows 9 to 13, 27 to 29, 32, 66 to 75) are the least work to bring back: their rows join the matrix as they stand. Tables and charts come next because the research lists both as weekly (`07-sales-users.md` rows "Add a table of numbers", "Add a chart of numbers"); they need their own audit first, and the GT brand deck carries neither block today (2.2). Image by URL, the Dither controls, the grid view's tile drag and click, and the JPEG and PNG rows come back with their fixes (`audit-images` summary items 3 and 4; `audit-slides` section 2.2 items 4 and 6; `audit-export` item 1). The shape galleries come back with the geometry interpreter (section 4).
- Two keys on the later list. `view.showSpeakerNotes` carries no shortcut on production (`model.ts` 1122 to 1125 has no `key`) while research 07's shortcut table lists Cmd+Option+Shift+S for the notes pane; production binds that chord to a focus move into the notes (`key.openNotes`, `EditorShell.tsx` 1405) rather than to the toggle, and the README (line 56) describes the focus move; the later item gives the row its key or documents the binding in the shortcuts dialog. Cmd+M adds no slide and says nothing (`audit-slides` row 8: six slides before and after, no snackbar) while Mac sellers try it; the later item shows the retired key sentence naming Ctrl+M (the pattern of `useEditorKeys.ts` 196 to 206 for the retired letters).
- Round five: motion, media, PPTX import, page setup, print, ODP, SVG, spelling, equations, themes, chat, the sync engine rework and the font catalog. It is not on production. In this checkout it is the uncommitted work on `main` at `d5a1be5` (`git status` lists the modified files; the working tree's `model.ts` flips `view.motion`, `insert.audio`, `insert.video`, `insert.templates`, `insert.buildingBlocks`, `slide.transition`, `help.training`, `help.updates`, `tools.spelling.spellCheck`, `tools.preferences`, `title.star` and others to Now that production holds as Later or Omit), and no branch named `round-five/integration` exists yet (`git branch -a`). The integrator moves that work to `round-five/integration`; this document ran no git write command. Round five's rows come back feature by feature under the rule below, never as one merge.
- The rule for bringing a feature back: its interactions are written as matrix rows with stable ids, a `feature` and a driver; the rows are driven on a preview and on production and pass; the ship note lists them; then, and only then, its rows lose the `advanced` flag. A feature returns whole or not at all: one not driven or failed row keeps every row of the feature parked.

## 9. Open questions for Kevin, and the decisions this revision made

Decided here, so they are no longer questions: the Later stubs hide with the parked set through `isPresent` (3.1); `toolbar.font` stays visible and disabled with its sentence as the one exception (3.1, 3.3); Insert > Table and Insert > Chart are parked, the tables a core layout places are text, and a chart a deck carries is edited under Advanced tools until a charts audit runs (2.2, 3.2); sharing's ship condition is enforce mode with the access record, and the fallback at the ship is sharing parked with the PDF named as the safe send (section 5, rank 1). Every rejection and addition of the two judgments is answered in the sections above; none is deferred.

1. Shapes at the ship. If the `shapes.*` battery is not all passing by the ship, section 4 parks the whole of Insert > Shape and Line and Arrow stand alone when their own rows pass. Ship without any shape in the default view for that release, or hold the ship until the rectangle, the rounded rectangle and the ellipse pass?
2. The access record's default when enforce mode turns on (section 5, rank 1). Anyone with the link can view, so the seller's View link keeps working with no step, or Restricted, Google's default (research 07 rule 18 and design rule 9), which adds one sharing step per deck before a prospect can open the link?
3. Who drives the not driven rows of 5.1 before the ship: the round's builders as assigned there, or Kevin by hand for the steps headless Chromium cannot drive (the browser's print dialog and its Save as PDF, `audit-export` row 33)?
